editorial:
Imagine a high-powered CEO who has her whole life planned out but is totally stressed out by the daily grind. That is Seon-wu, a fashion boss who lives and breathes her work. Then enter Ki-ho, a retired gentleman with a lifetime of wisdom who joins her company as a silver intern. At first, you will see a huge clash between Seon-wu's fast-paced digital world and Ki-ho's old-school way of doing things. The vibe is super cozy and heartwarming, making you feel like you are just hanging out with two people who are slowly becoming the best of friends despite their age gap.

What really makes this work is the chemistry between the leads; their conversations feel real and not forced. The pacing is steady, giving you plenty of laughs and a few tear-jerking moments. While the plot is pretty predictable, it is the small, sweet details that keep you invested.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Seon-wu learns to balance her career and personal life thanks to Ki-ho's guidance. She stops pushing herself to the breaking point and finds a healthier way to lead her company. Ki-ho does not stay as an intern forever but becomes a lifelong mentor and friend to her. The movie wraps up with a touching scene where they both realize that age does not matter when it comes to learning and growing.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about unlikely friendships and life lessons.
